subject: System Design
title: Single-Leader Replication
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Single-Leader Replication.

hook.text: All writes go to one leader. The leader copies them to followers. Reads can go to any node.

buildup.text: Single-leader replication is the simplest model. PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MongoDB all default to it.

discovery.text: It's easy to reason about: the leader has the authoritative copy. Conflicts are impossible on writes.

twist.text: The leader is a single point of failure. If it dies, a failover is needed — and failovers can lose recent writes.

climax.text: Single-leader is the go-to for most systems. It's simple, battle-tested, and good enough for most workloads.

punchline.text: One writer, many readers — simple and proven.

quiz.question: What is the main weakness of single-leader replication?
options: The leader is a single point of failure
